Method of Attack: Data wiper and info-stealer using ransomware as a decoy to steal files from macOS users
Installs a keylogger and opens a reverse shell
Checks for virtual machine environment and anti-debug capabilities
Checks for security tools and antimalware solutions
Connects to command-and-control server to download further files and send data
Distributed as trojanized installers of legitimate software wrapped in infected .PKG installers from torrent sites
Copies itself to ~/Library/AppQuest/com.apple.questd and creates a launch agent for persistence
Encrypts files appending a BEBABEDD marker, creates ransom note and uses text-to-speech to notify users
Steals files with specific extensions under /Users folder by downloading and executing Python scripts disguised as GIF files
Exfiltrates stolen files base64 encoded to remote URL
Uses static Bitcoin address for ransom payment without contact method, indicating ransomware is a wiper
Discoverer: K7 Lab malware researcher Dinesh Devadoss
Malwarebytes' Director of Mac & Mobile Thomas Reed
Jamf Principal Security Researcher Patrick Wardle
Attack Vector: Trojanized installers of popular apps downloaded from torrent trackers
Infected .PKG installers distributed as DMG files on torrent sites
Indicators of Compromise: Files copied to ~/Library/AppQuest/com.apple.questd and launch agent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.questd.plist
Encrypted files appended with BEBABEDD marker
